title: A Battery Made from a Single Material

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly identifies the target material as Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) multiple times, including in the main text (“Li10GeP2S12 was used as a model material…”) and in the Experimental Section (“Synthesis: Li10GeP2S12 was prepared…”). Therefore the extracted Target Formula is directly supported.

The extracted value for “Target Formula” is blank, but the paper explicitly identifies the target/single material repeatedly as Li10GeP2S12 (abbreviated LGPS), including in Figure 1 caption (“single-Li10GeP2S12”), throughout the text, and in the Experimental Section (“Synthesis: Li10GeP2S12 was prepared…”). Therefore a blank value is not supported by the source text.

The paper does mention lithium sulfide (Li2S) as a starting material in the Experimental Section and explicitly gives its molar ratio in the precursor mix (Li2S/P2S5/GeS2 = 5/1/1). Therefore, it is incorrect to say the amount is “not specified in text.” However, the text does not provide a mass or volume amount for Li2S, only purity and molar ratio.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Lithium sulfide (Li2S) — used as starting material; weighed in molar ratio Li2S/P2S5/GeS2 = 5/1/1 (no explicit mass given).

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper mentions P2S5 (phosphorus pentasulfide) as a starting material in the Experimental Section, but it also explicitly states the amount used via a molar ratio: “Li2S (…), P2S5 (…), and GeS2 (…) … weighed in the molar ratio of Li2S/P2S5/GeS2 = 5/1/1.” Therefore, the claim that the amount is “Not specified in text” is not correct.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Phosphorus pentasulfide (P2S5) | Amount: present as starting material, weighed in molar ratio Li2S:P2S5:GeS2 = 5:1:1 (no absolute mass given).

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper’s “Experimental Section” and main text do not identify the chemical as “Germanium disulfide” as the subject material. Instead, the studied/synthesized material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). GeS2 (germanium disulfide) is mentioned only as a starting material (“GeS2 ... were used as starting materials”) with a specified molar ratio (Li2S/P2S5/GeS2 = 5/1/1) and later as an anode analog (“GeS2 is a well-accepted anode...”), so the chemical identity/amount statement is incorrect. Also, the text does provide amounts (e.g., 10 mg LGPS–C, 120 mg LGPS, 30 mg LGPS–C) in the electrochemistry section, so “Amount: Not specified” is not accurate if referring to GeS2 or to the overall materials used.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Chemical identity should be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). If the intent is the GeS2 reagent: it is used as a starting material in molar ratio Li2S/P2S5/GeS2 = 5/1/1 (no absolute mass given). If the intent is cell component amounts: e.g., all-solid-state full cell uses 10 mg LGPS–C (anode), 120 mg LGPS (electrolyte), 30 mg LGPS–C (cathode).

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper clearly specifies the conductive additive used is carbon black and provides explicit amounts/ratios in multiple places (e.g., “LGPS:carbon is 75:25 in weight”; composite electrodes prepared with LGPS and carbon black 75:25; and specific masses such as 10 mg LGPS–C powder with 120 mg LGPS, and 10/120/30 mg for anode/electrolyte/cathode). Therefore the statement “Amount: Not specified in text” is contradicted by the source.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Carbon black | Amount: 25 wt% relative to LGPS in LGPS–C composite (LGPS:carbon = 75:25 by weight). (Also, for specific cells: LGPS–C powder masses of 10 mg (half-cell electrode), and 10 mg anode + 30 mg cathode in the full cell; plus 10 wt% PVDF binder in slurry electrodes.)

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper’s Experimental Section explicitly states the binder: “10 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and n-methylpyrrolidinone (NMP) to make the electrode slurries.” Thus PVDF is present and its amount is specified (10 wt%), contradicting the extracted claim that the amount is not specified.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) | Amount: 10 wt% (in electrode slurry formulation)

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The Experimental Section explicitly lists “n-methylpyrrolidinone (NMP)” as a component used to make electrode slurries (“mixed with 10 wt% polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and n-methylpyrrolidinone (NMP) to make the electrode slurries.”). However, no quantity/amount for NMP is given anywhere in the provided text (no mass, volume, concentration, or ratio for NMP), so “Amount: Not specified in text” is correct.

The paper explicitly states the liquid electrolyte composition as “1 M lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) in tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether (TEGDME) and n-methyl-(n-butyl) pyrrolidinium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PYR13TFSI)” (Page 4; also repeated in Experimental Section). This supports the chemical identity (LiTFSI) and the amount (1 M).

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly mentions tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether (TEGDME) as part of the liquid electrolyte: “1 M LiTFSI in tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether (TEGDME) and n-methyl-(n-butyl) pyrrolidinium … (PYR13TFSI)” and later “1 M LiTFSI in a mixture of 1:1 volume ratio of TEGDME and PYR13TFSI”. Therefore, the identity is supported and the ‘Amount: Not specified in text’ is also supported under the null-handling rule.

The paper explicitly mentions the ionic liquid component n-methyl-(n-butyl) pyrrolidinium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PYR13TFSI) as part of the liquid electrolyte (Page 4 and again in Experimental Section: “1 M LiTFSI in a mixture of 1:1 volume ratio of TEGDME and PYR13 TFSI”). However, the text provides only a 1:1 volume ratio with TEGDME and does not specify an absolute amount (mass/volume/moles) of PYR13TFSI used. Therefore, the ‘Amount: Not specified in text’ is correctly extracted.

The paper explicitly mentions use of lithium metal in multiple places (e.g., Li/LGPS/Pt cell; Li/LGPS/LGPS–C half-cells; “using a lithium metal foil as the counter electrode”; “a 100 µm thick lithium metal was then attached ... as a counter and reference electrode”). However, the text does not specify the *amount/mass* of lithium metal used—only a thickness (100 µm) and that it is a foil/counter electrode. Therefore the identity “Lithium metal” is supported and “Amount: Not specified in text” is also supported under the null-handling rule.

The Experimental Section explicitly states: “These materials were weighed in the molar ratio of Li2S/P2S5/GeS2 = 5/1/1 …” indicating that weighing is a synthesis operation performed during preparation of Li10GeP2S12.

The paper explicitly describes a mixing step in the synthesis and electrode preparation, e.g., starting materials “mixed for 30 min using a high-energy vibrating mill” and LGPS/carbon composites made by “hand-grinding” or “ball-milled for 20 h” to mix LGPS with carbon. This supports the synthesis operation being a mix step.

The paper explicitly describes pressing as part of synthesis/cell fabrication. In Experimental Section (Synthesis) it states “The powder obtained was then pressed into pellets…”. In Electrochemistry it also mentions “cold-pressed” assembly steps (e.g., “cold-pressed together under 360 MPa” and “direct cold-pressing…”). Thus the extracted synthesis operation “press” is supported.

The paper describes synthesis steps including weighing, milling, pressing into pellets, and explicitly states the pellets were "sealed in an evacuated quartz tube at 30 Pa" before heating. However, it does not describe a synthesis operation simply as "seal" in a standalone or generalized way; sealing is only mentioned as part of “sealed in an evacuated quartz tube”. Thus the extracted operation term "seal" is not explicitly stated in the text as such (only the phrase “sealed …”).
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: sealed in an evacuated quartz tube (at 30 Pa)

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The Experimental Section explicitly states the synthesis includes a heating step: the pressed pellets were “sealed in an evacuated quartz tube… and heated at 550 °C for 8 h in a furnace.” This supports the extracted synthesis operation “heat.”

The paper’s Experimental Section describes synthesis steps such as mixing, pressing into pellets, sealing, heating at 550 °C for 8 h, and then “naturally cooled down to the ambient temperature.” Nowhere does it explicitly state a synthesis operation described as “cool” (as a discrete step/operation name). The closest matching operation is “naturally cooled down,” which is not explicitly the word “cool.”
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: naturally cooled down to the ambient temperature

Provenance “Figure 2c” is consistent with the surrounding description.

This appears in the discussion of Figure 2d (“stable at a high potential up to 5.0 V”) and the Figure 2 caption notes the CV voltage range up to 5.0 V.
